subject: soviet submarine
title: In 1989 the Soviet Union Paid Pepsi With 17 Submarines

scenes.text: In 1989, a soda company got a fleet of submarines.
Pepsi had sold in the USSR since 1974, paid in vodka, because rubles couldn't leave the country.
By 1989, vodka wasn't enough. So: 17 old submarines, a cruiser, a frigate and a destroyer.
Pepsi's boss told the White House: we're disarming the Soviets faster than you are.
The ships went straight to a Norwegian scrapyard, each sub worth 150,000 dollars.
Sixth biggest navy on Earth, as the legend says? No. But for one spring, soda bought submarines.

description:
In the spring of 1989 the Soviet Union paid PepsiCo for its soda with 17 old submarines, a cruiser, a frigate and a destroyer.
Pepsi had been sold in the USSR since 1974 under a barter deal for Stolichnaya vodka, because Soviet rubles could not be used abroad. The 1989 warships were passed almost immediately to a Norwegian firm for scrap, with each submarine valued at about 150,000 dollars, and Pepsi chief Donald Kendall joked to US national security adviser Brent Scowcroft that Pepsi was disarming the Soviet Union faster than the government. The popular claim that Pepsi briefly had the sixth largest navy in the world is a myth: the ships were obsolete and Pepsi never operated them.
What's the strangest thing you've heard of being used as payment?
first_comment: A year later, in 1990, Pepsi signed a 3 billion dollar deal paid partly in Soviet tankers and freighters. Would you take a submarine as payment?
